findings.title: Four of the 14 identity assertions cannot fail on their own and are not labeled as regression guards
findings.evidence: At b439728 these four checks are already guaranteed by the read RPC's 'ready' path or by the schema. (1) #115 'review names the finalized task' (docs/release/ovd-520-staged-proof.sql:97): api_read_native_step_review returns 'taskId',t.id, where t is selected by id=p_task_id (ovd-563-step-review-forward.sql:168,208), and the segment passes pg_temp.task(1,31) as p_task_id. (2) #119 'review attempt is the finalized attempt': the RPC raises an integrity failure unless review.attempt_id = f.attempt_id (forward.sql:198). (3) #123 'review candidate is the conversation head': the RPC requires c.head_snapshot_id = f.snapshot_id = review.candidate_snapshot_id (forward.sql:185-186,200). (4) #127 'exactly one finalization': native_finalizations.task_id is unique (ovd-561-finalization-forward.sql:20), and the review row's foreign key requires that row to exist. #593 labeled its guards of this kind in a comment (staged-proof.sql:142-144 and 153-154); this segment does not. The issue's scope lists these checks, so including them is correct.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short SQL comment, as #593 did, marking #115, #119, #123 and #127 as regression guards implied by the 'ready' read and the schema. Optionally say so in the PR body's assertion table.

findings.title: The PR body's section I mapping claims more than the assertions check
findings.evidence: Row 1 of the PR body table maps 'review status is ready' to 'STEP export ID, source commit, report and STEP SHA-256'. Neither the segment nor the RPC checks export_id, source_commit or report_sha256. The RPC only compares step_sha256 with the stored bytes (forward.sql:205) and passes the other three through unchecked (forward.sql:211-212). Row 3 maps the message-body trace to 'Conversation, message and request IDs; interpretation ID; decision ID'. Assertion #116 only compares the joined message body with 'Depth 7 mm' and asserts no ID values. This is a documentation precision problem, not a code defect. The issue's acceptance criteria do not require the mapping; it was coordinator guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Change row 1 to 'STEP SHA-256 matches the stored bytes (RPC ready path); export ID, source commit and report SHA-256 are not asserted'. Change row 3 to say the IDs are linked through joins and only the message body is asserted.

findings.title: The acceptance-criterion mutation fails through the existing read RPC check, not through a new assertion (disclosed in the PR body)
findings.evidence: The spec's literal variant (immutability trigger disabled only) fails at the UPDATE with a foreign-key error (23503), as the PR body says. In variant 1b the run fails because the OVD-563 RPC raises ovd563_review_integrity_failure, not because a new assertion reports 'not ok'. I reproduced 1b in my worktree (fixture 368422b1): stage ovd520_staged_proof, '42501: ovd563_review_integrity_failure ... api_read_native_step_review line 57'. The criterion ('makes the run fail') is met. My own mutation run, described under checks_run, shows that the new trace assertions are genuinely discriminating.
findings.suggested_fix: None required. Optionally add a sentence to the PR body recording a direct mutation of the trace tables, like the one in checks_run.
